title: He Crushed 123 Bug Eggs and Stole a Dead Kid's Power . . . (Part 2)

segments.say: Dokja borrows his dead enemy's power, and one stab drops a screaming *zombie*.
To see how it got here, go back to Namwoon Kim's team-up offer, the *safe* choice.
But Dokja read this kid's whole story, and he *hated* the guy.
So Namwoon says get out of my way, he has business with that *granny*, but Dokja grabs his wrist.
Namwoon sneers that Dokja is playing hero, and the game says he now *despises* him.
Then Namwoon wakes his skill, and one slam sends Dokja crashing *backward*.
Then Dokja's head starts pounding, and a message says he just unlocked *Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint*.
Now he reads Namwoon's moves, and the kid can't land a single *hit*. Bro is basically Neo.
So Namwoon eyes the old lady, because if she dies he clears the scenario, and he *throws* a knife.
Dokja dives in front of her and carries her away, and the blade burns his *skin*.
The strong eat the weak, Namwoon says, and Dokja admits it. If he hesitates, he *dies*.
Dokja asks if an insect egg counts as an organism, then crushes the sack in his *fist*.
The system dings like crazy, because a grasshopper lays over a hundred eggs at a time. That was *savage*.
Dokja puts twenty-seven hundred coins into stamina, and Namwoon's knife suddenly can't *touch* him.
Namwoon swings and screams, why won't you die? Dokja says it's *Namwoon* who will.
Then the timer hits zero. Namwoon never killed a thing, so the game *takes* him.
Before that, Namwoon begged Dokja to save him. Dokja threw his own rule back: a new world needs *new rules*.
Then he wipes the blood off his face and wonders why he feels so *calm*. Cold, but it worked.
He wiped out a hundred and twenty-four living things, and the coins and a *title* pour in.
Then the train starts moving, everyone cheers, and a giant sea *serpent* explodes out of the water.
In the novel, Namwoon killed almost everyone in this cabin. Dokja just *rewrote* that.
Sanga asks if he's okay, and Dokja says sorry he couldn't save the old *lady*.
Then the goblin pops back in, thrilled, because twenty-one constellations are watching his *channel*.
Dokja spots a little boy, Gilyeong, alone in the corner, and asks him, do you want to *live*?
Let's team up, he says. It's not sympathy. If he had to name it, it's *hypocrisy*.
The constellations love it and tip him two hundred coins. Shameless, but it *works*.
Mr. Han asks to go home, but the goblin points at the serpent, and he admits they're all *grasshoppers*.
Every survivor can now get a sponsor, but nobody knows what that is. Nobody except Dokja, the only *reader* here.
Then four constellations pop up on his screen, and the novel's hero only started with *five*.
One is a dragon he doesn't know. Two is a fire demon that's secretly an *archangel*.
Three is a hooded shadow he's never read about. Four is the Great Sage, who crushes hundreds in one *swing*.
Then the goblin ends the selection and says someone made a very *interesting* choice.
He leaves for ten minutes to prep the next scenario, and Hyeonseong walks over to shake Dokja's *hand*.
Hyeonseong thanks him for saving them, then Mr. Han slaps his shoulder and calls him *rookie*.
Mr. Han blows up about bugs, so Hyeonseong tells him to *shut up* and wake up. That company doesn't even exist.
Then Dokja asks who still doesn't get it. Nobody argues, because this isn't a dream, it's *reality*.
So Dokja says they have to get out, but Mr. Han calls him crazy, and then something *slams* the door from the other side.
Dokja knows who it is, the sole survivor of cabin thirty-seven oh seven, the guy who killed his whole *cabin*.
Every door in the cabin is *broken*, and the last one only creaks open an inch.
Dokja tells Hyeonseong to just *imagine* his skill, and he roars, glows green, and it works.
Dokja groans that he knew this would happen, and the goblin blasts in, furious they didn't stay *put*.
He sighs and starts the second scenario early. Cross the collapsed bridge in twenty minutes, or pay a *mystery* penalty.
The bridge is still standing, but Dokja knows it will collapse, so he tells everyone to *run*.
Then the water starts to spin, and a sea serpent explodes out beside them.
The goblin grins that it's too easy, so he cranks the difficulty, and the dead crawl out of the *ground*.
They run down the stairs with the horde behind them, the serpent snaps at Dokja, and he goes down *hard*.
Then a constellation steps in, and a bridge of light appears. Only an *even* number of people can cross it.
That's a rare trick, even in the novel. But when Dokja tries to read Sanga's profile, his skill gets *blocked*.
Then someone yells *behind you*, and a demon crashes in, wearing a name tag that says Namwoon Kim.
Of course it's him. And Dokja's skill fails, because a zombie has no *mind* left to read.
The bridge only takes two, but there are three of them, so one has to stay behind and *die*.
Mr. Han grabs Sanga and drags her across, and Dokja is left *behind*, alone. Real friendly, Mr. Han.
Dokja is alone with fifteen minutes left, and when the goblin asks who'll bless this poor guy, nobody *answers*.
Zombies close in, Dokja wishes for one combat skill, and then a new skill, *Bookmark*, lights up.
In three thousand chapters of the novel, he never read about it, but he somehow *knows* how it works.
It saves characters he understands, and Namwoon Kim sits in slot number *one*.
Dokja whispers, activate bookmark number one, and a purple flood of the dead kid's power *pours* in.
Then he stabs the zombie with Namwoon's own skill, and the monster *drops*.
Namwoon croaks that he doesn't want to die, while Dokja just *stares* at him, glowing purple.
Dokja's skill shuts off, the clock says ten minutes, and he's waiting on one man who should be here *already*.
Then a shockwave rips through the horde, and zombies fly in every *direction*.
Dokja looks up and whispers *there he is*. The man he has been waiting for just walked in.
